One of the witnesses, speaking of what a girl was doing at the time the assault took place, said she was ‘badding’ walnuts in a pigstye. The word is peculiarly provincial: to ‘bad’ walnuts is to strip away the husk. The walnut, too, is often called a ‘bannut,’ and hence the old Gloucestershire phrase, ‘Come an’ bad the bannuts.’

glosses: Marked by pessimism and little hopefulness; expecting the worst.

examples.text: a pessimistic view of the future
a pessimistic estimate
However pessimistic their predictions, most scientists and scholars who warn of impending disaster are really acting from antidystopian motives.

glosses: Taking out exclusive locks on data to prevent conflicts with other processes that might modify it.

examples.text: pessimistic concurrency; pessimistic locking

The lawyer and twice-divorced mother of three had presented herself as the modern face of her party, trying to strip it of unsavoury overtones after her father's convictions for saying the Nazi occupation of France was not "particularly inhumane".

England consolidated their position of power in pursuit of a place at next year's World Cup in Qatar with a hugely impressive victory against Hungary in a hostile and often unsavoury atmosphere in Budapest.

glosses: Disreputable, not respectable, of questionable moral character.

examples.text: His unsavory reputation as a mobster came back to haunt him when he ran for mayor of New York.
The case against Khela rested primarily on the testimony of two unsavoury witnesses, [who] had lengthy criminal records and [...] were members of a prison-based gang.
